newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra cuts 1996/97 housing forecast to 125,600.
newsitem.headline: Canberra cuts 1996/97 housing forecast to 125,600.

text.p: The Australian government's housing adviser, the Indicative Planning Council for the Housing Industry, on Tuesday lowered its 1996/97 (July-June) forecast to 125,600 from the previous 127,000 forecast.
The council also forecast 143,000 housing starts for the following year, to June 30, 1998.
The industry commenced construction of 124,532 houses dwellings in 1995/96.
"The (council) agreed the recovery in the housing industry had begun as expected at its last meeting in October 1996," the council said in a statement, reporting on its Tuesday meeting.
"This is confirmed by the rise in seasonally adjusted dwelling commencements in the December quarter 1996 and by further rises in forward indicators of activity for the March quarter 1997."
The council also estimated that Australia would need about 141,600 dwellings a year to satisfy demand until 2000/01.
In theory, this could be partly satisfied by a surplus stock, such as the 21,000 surplus that existed in June 1996.
But the council estimated that that surplus would have disappeared and turned into pent-up demand for 4,700 dwellings by the end of June 1997.
